note: Window agent m0400-m0301, 2 Nov 2026. Cyrenaica keyframes of the Ptolemies (gazetteer region too wide), Scythia east of the Don until 313, the upper satrapies (Sogdia, Bactria, Mesopotamia) kept in the Macedonian empire 331-309 and in the Seleucid empire from 301, Qin's Sichuan gain a year early, Alexander's limit at the Beas.

region.text: the rest of the Sichuan basin in Cliopatria's Qin shape of 315: the land between and around the Shu and Ba cells (808 cells); without the Hanzhong cells (place Hanzhong 80 km) that the qin_-315 keyframe leaves out until the 312 gain from Chu

events.note: 316: Qin completes the conquest of Shu and Ba. 'In 316 BC, Qin completed the conquests of the southern states of Ba and Shu, in modern Sichuan.' The dossier's gains from shu and ba (ledger 15, 16) take only the 587 cells those two states drew; the other 808 cells of the Sichuan basin in the Qin shape stay empty until the 315 keyframe snap, a year late. [review m0400-m0301: Hanzhong 80 km cut from the region, as in keyframe qin_-315, so that 5 Sichuan cells near Hanzhong do not flicker to Qin in 316 and out again in 315.]

region.text: the left (east and south) bank of the Don inside the Scythian 404 shape: Volgograd, Saratov, Tambov, eastern Voronezh, southern Rostov and the strip south of the Don mouth (655 cells; the polygon's west edge follows the Don)

events.note: Added by the reviewer of m0400-m0301 to narrow keyframe_overrides/6-7: the Sarmatians page says 'By the 5th century BC the Sarmatians held control of the land between the Urals and the Don River', and that only after the Scythian defeats of 339 and 313 'the Sarmatians began crossing the Don river and invaded Scythia'. So the left bank is not Scythian in this window (the Sarmatian dossier starts only in 313, so it is nobody's until then); the right-bank part of the 404 shape (Ukraine, Kursk, Belgorod, western Voronezh, northern Rostov, 905 cells) stays Scythian until 313 as keyframe_overrides/6-7 intend. Dated -400, the window's first year, because the page puts the Sarmatian hold in the 5th century.

correction.text: Egypt and the Pentapolis of Cyrenaica (Cliopatria's Cyrenaica shape, 103 cells), subjugated by Ptolemy's general Ophellas in 322

keyframe_overrides.why: The keyframe adds {'region': 'Cyrenaica'}, which the gazetteer resolves to 2,496 cells (631,000 km2) because it follows the modern definition: the Cyrenaica page says 'Cyrenaica includes all of the eastern part of Libya between the 16th and 25th meridians east, including the Kufra District'. For antiquity the same page says 'the more important western portion was known as the Pentapolis' and 'In the south, the Pentapolis faded into the Saharan tribal areas'. Replaced by the Cliopatria Cyrenaica shape (103 cells, 30,697 km2 around the Pentapolis) that the cyrenaica dossier itself draws; otherwise the draft gives Ptolemy the whole Kufra desert (1,404 cells) from 322. Same correction text as the dossier, region narrowed.

Sarmatians page: Scythians 'were militarily defeated by the Macedonian kings Philip II of Macedon and Lysimachus in 339 and 313 BCE respectively'. correction.text: the smaller Cliopatria shape (Ukraine, Moldova and the Don bend), from 313: the steppe east of the Don is still Scythian, contested from 339, until the Sarmatian conquest of 313

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own ledger keeps the steppe east of the Don Scythian and contested from 339 (scythia/ledger/12) and hands it to the Sarmatians in 313 (ledger/14, a loss to sarmatians); the keyframe note says the Sarmatians began crossing the Don only 'After Scythian defeats in 339 and 313 BC'. The Sarmatians page: the Scythians 'were militarily defeated by the Macedonian kings Philip II of Macedon and Lysimachus in 339 and 313 BCE respectively' and were 'the then dominant power in the Black Sea Steppe' at the end of the 4th century. But the compiler snaps to the smaller Cliopatria shape in -350, so the 1,560 cells east of the Don (Volgograd, Rostov, Voronezh) are dropped 37 years early and the 339 contest and the 313 loss act on nothing. The keyframe now starts in 313, when the ledger moves the land. [review m0400-m0301: the 1,560 cells are not all east of the Don: 905 lie on its right (west) bank (Ukraine 333, Kursk 121, Belgorod 117, western Voronezh, northern Rostov) and stay Scythian to 313 under this override; the 655 left-bank cells, which the same page gives to the Sarmatians from the 5th century BC ('By the 5th century BC the Sarmatians held control of the land between the Urals and the Don River'), are cut from -400 by events/1.]

correction.text: the Balkan homeland, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and Egypt (Cliopatria's mislabelled 'Ptolemaic Kingdom' shape of 331-327), and Mesopotamia with Babylonia and Susiana after Gaugamela (1 October 331: 'He then advances to Babylon and Susa'); the ledger adds Persis and Media (330), the eastern satrapies (330) and Bactria-Sogdia (329-327)

keyframe_overrides.why: Alexander the Great page: 'Leaving Egypt in 331 BC, Alexander marched eastward into Achaemenid Assyria in Upper Mesopotamia' and 'defeated Darius again at the Battle of Gaugamela'; Babylon was captured after it. The dossier's own ledger (macedonian-empire/ledger/30) gives Mesopotamia, Babylonia and Khuzestan in 331, but the keyframe lists only Babylonia and Khuzestan, so the 331 snap strips 1,159 cells (Al-Anbar 164, Ninawa 118 and others) to nobody until the -326 keyframe returns them. Mesopotamia added to the keyframe, as in keyframe -326.

correction.text: the empire of the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV under the regent Perdiccas (Partition of Babylon, June 323), without the satrapies Cliopatria already draws as rows of their own (Thrace, Syria, Babylonia), and with the Sogdian, Bactrian and Mesopotamian land Cliopatria's shape lacks; Egypt stays inside to 320

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's Macedonian shape lacks about 560 Sogdian and 230 Bactrian cells and the Mesopotamian desert (the -325 keyframe says so: 'Cliopatria's shape lacks about 560 Sogdian, 230 Bactrian, 720 Mesopotamian and 470 Punjab cells'), but this keyframe does not add them back, so the compiler drops them to nobody in 323 and they stay empty until the Seleucid keyframe of 309 (Navoi 363, Al-Anbar 355 cells and others; 2,148 cells unowned at the end of 323). Triparadisus page, table of satraps: at the Partition of Babylon (323) Bactria and Sogdiana 'Philip' and Mesopotamia 'Arcesilaus' (Diodorus); at Triparadisus (321) Bactria 'Stasanor', Sogdiana 'Stasanor', Mesopotamia 'Amphimachus', Babylonia 'Seleucus': satrapies of the empire throughout 323-316. [review m0400-m0301: the 323 satraps were wrongly given as 'same men'; the quote about dispossessing those confirmed by Alexander concerns Taxiles on the Hydaspes and is dropped.] Added: Sogdia, Bactria and Mesopotamia as the dossier's own ledger (macedonian-empire/ledger/30, 33) and keyframe -325 hold them; Babylonia stays out where another state holds it.

keyframe_overrides.why: Seleucid Empire page: Seleucus 'was easily able to establish control and conquer the Upper Satrapies' (c. 310); under Antiochus II 'Bactria and Sogdiana simultaneously asserted their independence' under Diodotus, so both were Seleucid until then; the page names only Gedrosia and Arachosia and the Indus lands as ceded to Chandragupta. Runs to 292 (next window); seleucid-empire_-291 (ok, Cliopatria shape) will cut them again from 291.

region.text: Haryana and Rajasthan, east of the Beas

rulings.why: Alexander the Great page: 'Alexander's army mutinied at the Hyphasis River (Beas), refusing to march farther east.' 'This river thus marks the easternmost extent of Alexander's conquests.' Haryana and Rajasthan lie beyond the Beas and stay the Nanda realm's; the Punjab region of the Macedonian keyframes reaches them.
